A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SURE framework and spurious-feature robustness study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original statistical experiments, Mistral and Llama robustness evaluations, and model-family and scaling comparisons, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds open-web evaluation, an LLM-judge comparison, prompting comparisons, and SFT/DPO training experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.4 introduces two mitigation procedures absent from v1: SFT on correct answers paired with original and perturbed passages, and DPO preferring correct over incorrect answers for both passages. This substantially extends the work from evaluation to model training. The original SURE perturbation and preservation pipeline remains intact.

E1.justification: V2 retains the NQ-open/Wikipedia coverage, naming the synthetic dataset SURE_Wiki and renaming SIG to SIG_Wiki. It adds SIG_Trivial using TriviaQA queries and longer, Bing-retrieved open-web documents, also used for out-of-domain evaluation of trained models. This materially broadens the represented retrieval environment beyond Wikipedia.

E2.justification: V2 adds comparisons of Chain-of-Note against plain Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1 against DeepSeek-V3 in Table 4. Table 5 additionally compares unmodified Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with SFT and DPO variants. These introduce substantive mitigation comparisons beyond v1's model benchmarking; the original six-model comparison remains.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampling 1,000 TriviaQA queries, three golden web documents per query, and 100 instances per perturbation subcategory; complementary evaluation using a two-demonstration, chain-of-thought Llama-3.1-70B judge; and two-epoch training on over 30,000 samples followed by in-domain and out-of-domain testing. The original RR/WR/LR definitions remain unchanged. Abbreviated descriptions of retained sampling do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a reliability analysis comparing string-based evaluation with an LLM judge, investigates prompting and reasoning as mitigation strategies, and tests SFT/DPO generalization between Wikipedia and open-web benchmarks. These address new measurement and robustness questions. The existing model-family and scaling analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The preliminary K-S tests retain their 0.05 significance threshold, statistics, and p-values, moving from v1 Appendix B to v2 Appendix A. Neither version reports benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new results do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding LR/RR/WR values in v1 Tables 2/6 and v2 Tables 1/9 are retained, while original/perturbed accuracy entries are added and aggregate results and Unknown-Noise LR/WR entries are removed. V2 Tables 3–5 add substantial new findings. For example, Table 5 newly reports SIG_Trivial style RR of 87.5 for unmodified Llama, 88.5 with SFT, and 94.5 with DPO. These are new experimental comparisons, not revisions of v1 scores.

T1.justification: The oracle-score and robustness-rate definitions, retrieval formulation, and causal/spurious feature distinction remain substantively unchanged. The dot-product equation is expressed in prose and the oracle discussion moves to the appendix. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, and conclusion expand the central purpose from quantifying robustness to improving it through synthetic-data training. Mitigation, identified as future work in v1, becomes a claimed achieved contribution in v2. Statistical identification remains supported but is no longer foregrounded as a separate principal contribution.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the main prior-knowledge/noise interaction discussion with an interpretation that robustness on golden documents is independent of internal knowledge. It adds interpretations concerning judge reliability, prompting limitations, and SFT versus DPO generalization, plus a qualification that timestamps can be causal in time-sensitive tasks. Conversely, it omits the oracle-score long-answer limitation and the explicit warning that RR can conceal changes between incorrect responses.

D1.justification: Appendices F–H add web-benchmark construction, judge implementation, training hardware, and hyperparameters, including learning rate 2e-5, effective batch size 32, and maximum sequence length 4096. V2 omits v1's Wikipedia snapshot date, explicit 500-known/500-unknown query selection, and preliminary answer-length restriction. The repository link remains, but its description changes from code and data to code only; this does not establish actual withdrawal of data access.

R1.justification: The two main related-work themes remain. V2 qualifies the research gap by acknowledging prior RAG studies of typos and formatting, adds Chain-of-Note and reasoning-model literature, and adds dataset citations while pruning several earlier references. These refine positioning without replacing the central distinction between explicit noise and spurious features.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: preliminary material moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, related work moves into Section 2, dataset discussion moves into experiments, and mitigation receives its own subsection. The abstract, introduction, contributions, result interpretations, and conclusion are rewritten, with new limitations and ethical-considerations sections.

P2.justification: The detailed model-result tables are redesigned with accuracy columns and reduced noise/aggregate columns, and four new tables present additional comparisons and training settings. Existing figures retain their underlying content but are resized or relocated. The document is extensively reformatted, including conversion of appendix prose from single-column to two-column layout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens external validity through open-web evaluation and adds a useful check of string-based scoring against an LLM judge. It also turns v1's proposed future mitigation work into documented training experiments. However, Table 5 reports only RR, which counts consistently incorrect answers as robust, and training/evaluation separation is not clearly documented. Together with omitted sampling details and metric caveats, these limitations constrain the overall quality gain despite the substantial expansion.
